newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban claims downing opposition warplane.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban claims downing opposition warplane.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia shot down an opposition warplane with a U.S.-made Stinger missile on Friday in the southwestern province of Badghis, a Taleban spokesman said.

The spokesman, quoted by a Pakistan-based Afghan news service, said the warplane belonging to the forces of northern Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum was hit by the shoulder-fired missile while bombing Taleban positions in the province's Bala Murghab area.
The plane began bombing the positions after the Taleban advanced on an opposition post.
The Taleban advanced about 10 km (six miles) to take the opposition post at Akazi village, the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted the Taleban spokesman in the western Afghan city of Herat as saying.
Between 20 and 25 of Dostum's forces were killed and 30 captured, he said. At least two Taleban fighters were killed.
The report could not be independently verified.

AIP quoted Herat governor Mullah Yar Mohammad as saying the Taleban had more Stinger missiles, which were supplied to the Afghan mujahideen guerrillas when fighting Soviet occupation in the 1980s, and would use them against opposition forces.
Last month, the Taleban said a former guerrilla commander had given it 19 Stingers in Sarobi town east of the capital Kabul.
Stringers proved to be the most effective weapon against the Soviet aircraft during the occupation.
The United States tried to recover unused stocks after the Soviet withdrawal but Afghans guarded them jealously.
